Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: zshijie-publisher
Version: 0.1.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate tool for managing content on the Z视介 (ZShiJie) platform. The primary script, `scripts/publisher_cli.py`, implements a standard QR-code login flow and content publishing API interactions with appropriate security considerations, such as redacting session IDs and cookies from console output. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found across the code or documentation.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and install steps are consistent with a CLI that logs in by QR and publishes/edits content to the documented Z视介 endpoints; it requests only python3 and does not ask for unrelated credentials or hidden endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the bundled code and docs: the Python CLI implements a QR login flow, extracts a sessionId, and performs publish/edit operations against the documented Z视介 endpoints. Required binary (python3) and the Homebrew install suggestion are proportional to that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructions map directly to the CLI behavior: generate QR HTML/PNG, wait for user scan, persist session file, and run publish/edit calls. The instructions do not request unrelated filesystem, environment, or network access beyond the documented temp files and the Z视介 endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install spec only offers installing Python via Homebrew (formula: python) on macOS; that's reasonable given the requirement for python3. Installing Python is heavyweight but expected; no arbitrary binary downloads or obscure URLs are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars/credentials. It stores a local session file (temp dir) and reuses sessionId for requests. The inclusion of a fixed client-side sign seed in code is explained in the docs as an implementation constant (not a secret) and is consistent with the QR polling flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false. The skill writes only its own session file and temporary QR artifacts (HTML/PNG) and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. The release helper runs external 'clawhub' or 'npx' only when executed explicitly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it generates a QR for you to scan on the official creator login page, extracts and stores a sessionId in a local session file, and then uses that sessionId to call Z视介 publish/edit endpoints (default host https://zugcpublish.cztv.com). Before installing, consider: (1) it requires network access to mp.cztv.com and zugcpublish.cztv.com so only run if you trust those endpoints; (2) the CLI will write a session file under the system temp directory and temporary QR files (HTML/PNG) — delete them if you no longer need the session; (3) the release_to_clawhub helper will call an external 'clawhub' or 'npx' command only if you run it with --execute, so do not run that unless you trust the publish target and have clawhub configured; (4) if you need higher assurance, inspect scripts/publisher_cli.py fully (it redacts session values in logs) and test with a non-production account first.
